facts.text: Cloister is the original heart of The Boca Raton and has welcomed guests since 1926.
facts.excerpt: The original heart of The Boca Raton, Cloister has been welcoming guests since 1926.

facts.text: Cloister is defined by Mediterranean-inspired architecture, secluded courtyards and lush tropical gardens.
facts.excerpt: Cloister has embodied the romance of South Florida, where Mediterranean-inspired architecture, secluded courtyards, and lush tropical gardens have created an unmistakable sense of place.

facts.text: Cloister's rooms were newly redesigned in fall 2026.
facts.excerpt: Newly redesigned rooms in fall 2026

facts.text: The redesigned guestrooms honor the hotel's architectural character through a fresh, modern lens, with playful details.
facts.excerpt: The guestrooms honor the hotel’s architectural character through a fresh, modern lens, with playful details that capture the vibrant spirit of The Boca Raton.

facts.text: Cloister features rotating art collections and fashion collaborations throughout.
facts.excerpt: Cloister is a place of discovery, with rotating art collections, fashion collaborations, and unexpected moments woven throughout.

facts.text: Cloister's central location puts the resort's historic Golf Club, its Racquet Club and Spa Palmera within easy reach.
facts.excerpt: Its central location puts some of the resort’s most celebrated experiences within easy reach, from our historic Golf Club and expansive Racquet Club to Forbes Five-Star Spa Palmera.

facts.text: Spa Palmera is described as Forbes Five-Star.
facts.excerpt: Forbes Five-Star Spa Palmera

facts.text: Cloister offers a location and accommodations suited to groups and families.
facts.excerpt: Ideal location and accommodations for groups and families

facts.text: Cloister guests have full resort access.
facts.excerpt: Full resort access

facts.text: Cloister guests have access to the private amenities of The Boca Raton Club.
facts.excerpt: Access to the private amenities of The Boca Raton Club

facts.text: Cloister is dog-friendly for dogs up to 35 pounds.
facts.excerpt: Dog-friendly (up to 35 pounds)

facts.text: Cloister guests have water taxi service.
facts.excerpt: Water taxi service

facts.text: Cloister offers a fleet of bicycles.
facts.excerpt: Fleet of bicycles

facts.excerpt: Molton Brown bath amenities

facts.text: Cloister's suites include the Mizner Suite.
facts.excerpt: Mizner Suite

facts.text: Cloister offers resort activity programming.
facts.excerpt: Resort activity programming

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler calls Cloister the resort's most classically designed stay, with dark-wood furnishings and inconspicuous artwork.
facts.excerpt: The Cloisters is the most classically designed stay, with dark-wood furnishings and inconspicuous artwork

facts.text: Cloister is the closest of the resort's stays to its main amenities, like dining and shopping.
facts.excerpt: plus it’s closest to all the resort’s main amenities, like dining and shopping.

facts.text: The Boca Raton began in 1926 as an inn built by architect Addison Mizner.
facts.excerpt: The Boca Raton began in 1926 as a 100-room inn that legendary architect Addison Mizner built with funding from the Ritz-Carlton.

facts.text: Spa Palmera is an ode to the Alhambra Palace, with arches, stonework, mosaic tiles and a courtyard with a lap pool.
facts.excerpt: An ode to the Alhambra Palace, Spa Palmera brings the majesty and feel of the Moorish castle to Florida, thanks to an expansive 50,000-square-foot spa replete with arches, stone work, mosaic tiles

facts.text: Two water taxis carry guests across Lake Boca Raton to the resort's private beachfront.
facts.excerpt: There are even two water taxis that transport guests to and from the Harborside location across Lake Boca Raton to the private beachfront.

facts.text: Mizner Park, an outdoor district with a fine arts museum, shopping and dining, is about a five-minute drive north of the resort.
facts.excerpt: A five-minute drive northward gets you to Mizner Park, an outdoor entertainment district with a fine arts museum, high-end shopping, and chef-driven dining.
